analysis.title: Amphenol Corp. (APH): Record results with broad-based growth, including robust AI/datacenter sales; 3Q26 wrap
key_insights: Amphenol's 3Q26 revenue of $10,230 mn and operating EPS of $0.80 were well above FactSet consensus ($9,491 mn / $0.73) and GS ($9,475 mn / $0.72). Revenue was up 17% qoq, 65% yoy and 37% yoy organically, against company guidance of $9,300-$9,400 mn.

4Q26 guidance midpoint of $10,400 mn revenue and $0.82 operating EPS is above the Street ($9,771 mn / $0.75) and GS prior ($9,899 mn / $0.76). Guidance excludes the not-yet-closed AdvancedPCB, Dexgreen and Humanetics Sensors acquisitions.
Management said AI now accounts for about 75% of IT datacom sales, which GS implies is $3.7-3.8 bn of AI revenue, against GS's 2Q26 estimate of $2.7-2.8 bn. That is roughly a $1 bn qoq increase.
Orders were a record $12.2 bn, a 1.19x book-to-bill, up 99% yoy and 13% qoq. All but one end market had a book-to-bill above 1.
Adjusted operating margin was 29.7% versus 29.1% for both GS and the Street. GS excludes the one-time IEEPA benefit from 2Q in calling this a record margin, and expects EBIT margins to trend higher.

Amphenol raised its 2026 CommScope outlook for the second straight quarter, to $5.1 bn of sales and $0.18 of EPS from $4.6 bn and $0.15. GS says this should help investors appreciate the company's fiber momentum in the datacenter.
IT & Data Communications revenue was $4,910 mn (48% of total), up 117% yoy and 77% organically. Industrial grew 60% yoy and 25% organically. Communications Networks fell 28% organically.

4Q26 end-market guidance: Mobile Devices +35% qoq, IT & Data Communications and Defense up mid-single digits, Commercial Aerospace flat at 3Q levels, Industrial somewhat lower, Automotive slightly lower, Communications Networks down further.
Free cash flow was about $1,623 mn (about 16% of revenue). The company spent $245 mn on buybacks and $308 mn on dividends in 3Q.
Amphenol raised its quarterly dividend to $0.15 from $0.125 and announced a new $4 bn 3-year buyback effective January 1. It expects to finish the remainder of its existing $2 bn plan by year-end.

Amphenol closed Empire Electronics (about $320 mn FY26 sales, automotive lighting) and signed deals for AdvancedPCB (about $270 mn), Dexgreen (about $90 mn) and Humanetics Sensors (about $70 mn). The three together cost about $1.6 bn, funded with cash and debt.

GS raised 2026/27/28 EPS estimates to $2.83/$3.90/$4.45 from $2.70/$3.50/$4.00. It raised the 12-month price target to $122 from $116, based on 28x (down from 30x, reflecting peer multiples) normalized EPS of $4.35. Buy rating maintained with 50.7% upside from $80.96.
Key downside risks are revenue growth, margins, the China trade situation given Amphenol's manufacturing sites there, and M&A execution.

market_movers.rationale: GS kept Buy and raised the target to $122 from $116 after a 3Q26 beat and a 4Q guide well above the Street. Estimates rose on higher revenue and margins.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees APH well positioned in both fiber and copper, with AI now about 75% of IT datacom sales.
GS names industrials and A&D, alongside datacenter, as end markets with secular and cyclical growth drivers for APH.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 revenue $10,229.7 mn reported vs GS est $9,475.1 mn and FactSet consensus $9,491.0 mn (beat of 8.0% vs GS and 7.8% vs Street). Company guidance was $9,300-$9,400 mn.
3Q26 non-GAAP operating EPS $0.80 reported vs GS est $0.72 and FactSet consensus $0.73. It was above the high end of company guidance of about $0.70-$0.71.
3Q26 non-GAAP operating income $3,036.3 mn reported vs GS est $2,754.2 mn and Street $2,763.0 mn. Adjusted operating margin was 29.7% vs 29.1% for both GS and the Street.

4Q26 guidance: revenue $10,300-$10,500 mn (midpoint $10,400 mn) vs GS prior est $9,899.1 mn and FactSet consensus $9,771.0 mn. EPS guidance $0.81-$0.83 (midpoint $0.82) vs GS prior est $0.76 and consensus $0.75.

GS 2026E/2027E/2028E EPS (diluted, pre-exceptionals) estimates are $2.83/$3.90/$4.45, up from $2.70/$3.50/$4.00. 2026E/2027E/2028E revenue estimates are $37,100 mn/$48,799 mn/$55,866 mn, up from $35,752 mn/$45,542 mn/$51,624 mn.
Orders were $12.2 bn reported for 3Q26, up 99.6% yoy and 13.7% qoq, with a 1.19x book-to-bill.
CommScope 2026 contribution raised to $5.1 bn of sales and $0.18 of EPS from $4.6 bn and $0.15.
risk_factors: Revenue growth could fall short of estimates.
Margins could come in below expectations.
The trade situation with China, given Amphenol's several manufacturing sites there.
Amphenol's ability to keep executing well on M&A.
geopolitical: The report lists the trade situation with China as a downside risk, given Amphenol's several manufacturing sites in the country.
